summary.headline: IKIO Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 169 crore and EBITDA rose 94% to Rs 22 crore, but gross margin fell to about 41% on war-driven component and metal costs.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 41% YoY to Rs 169 crore, led by the other businesses (Rs 124 crore, up 53% YoY but marginally lower QoQ) while home lighting ODM reached Rs 45 crore (up 16% YoY, 18% QoQ). EBITDA rose 94% YoY to Rs 22 crore (13% margin vs 9.4%) and PAT rose to Rs 11 crore from Rs 2 crore. Management said sequential profitability was hit by higher raw material and semiconductor costs linked to the Middle East war and by higher wages after a minimum wage revision. Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance at 18-20% and group EBITDA margin at 13-14%.

down from 44-45% as cited by analyst

segments.name: Other businesses (Lighting, Hearables & Wearables, Energy, Electronic components, Automotive lighting, non-lighting)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 124 crore, up 53% YoY; growth was broad-based across verticals except UAE/Gulf, which declined due to the war. Management said the war cost roughly Rs 10-15 crore of business in the quarter. Hearables and wearables contribute about 15-17% of total revenue.

segments.name: Home lighting ODM
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 45 crore, up 16% YoY and 18% QoQ. Customer concentration fell from about 95% from one customer to 3-4 customers. Management expects FY27 at roughly Rs 170 crore, plus or minus Rs 10-15 crore.

segments.name: Automotive lighting (aftermarket LED)
segments.commentary: Actual production began in May/June 2026 after prototyping and trials. Management says it is aligned with five industry-leading aftermarket LED brands. FY27 contribution is expected to be small.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance kept at 18-20%, as given in Q4; management will revisit by end-Q2 or Q3 if needed.
Group EBITDA margin guided at about 13-14% for FY27; management said it would be 14% or slightly better without the war.
ODM home lighting EBITDA margin expected to stay near 8.4%, give or take 0.5%, if raw material prices stay stable or fall.
Long-term feasible EBITDA margin cited at 17-18%, not the earlier 20-23%. Management targets asset turns of 4.5-5x in about 3-3.5 years.
Management expects raw material and wage pressure to normalise in coming quarters as revenue scale and operating leverage build.
Automotive OEM onboarding targeted by FY28, after aftermarket traction.
Honeywell SKUs expected to rise 3-4x by year-end.
capex_capacity: Block 1 (about 2 lakh sq ft) is operational; Block 2 (Tower-2) partially commercialised in Q2 FY27, with hearables and wearables using two floors.
Block 3 construction is on schedule; about Rs 20 crore of remaining capex is earmarked for Tower-3.
FY27 capex guided at about Rs 20-25 crore, with little left after Tower-2.
Depreciation from Tower-2 expected to start from Q2 FY27; management pointed to cash PAT for comparability.
demand_pricing: Semiconductor prices have roughly doubled in some cases, and lead times have risen from about 4-6 weeks to over a year for some electronic components, forcing spot buying and design changes.
Metals (MS, aluminium, copper) prices have been volatile over the past 4-5 months.
Management is in talks with customers on pricing to offset cost pressure.
Middle East/UAE business declined YoY due to the war, though management says IKIO is outperforming peers there and is entering the developer segment.
About 50% of hearables/wearables products are now IKIO-designed ODM products, up from job work.
Honeywell: amplifiers, PA systems and fire alarm panels are in production, with more products in the pipeline.
Solar inverter/BESS: one sizeable order completed; new products in development.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory given geopolitical and manpower headwinds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are in line with annual guidance. Gross margin was hit by component lead times and metal and semiconductor costs, and the company is negotiating with customers. Long-term feasible EBITDA margin is 17-18%, not 20-23%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall from 44-45% to 41%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed metal price volatility and semiconductor shortages and price spikes. It redesigned products to keep specs while avoiding shortages, and said 41% is sustainable at current raw material prices unless the war escalates.

qa_highlights.question: Was the other business QoQ dip due to seasonality or the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally the leanest quarter. YoY, Q1 FY27 Rs 124 crore matched the full Q1 FY26 base of about Rs 120 crore, and the war cost an estimated Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 40% growth in the home lighting ODM business and what is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: New customers were added and the customer base diversified from one customer to 3-4. Management expects FY27 at around Rs 170 crore, plus or minus Rs 10-15 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hearables and wearables production visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: H&W is about 15-16% of revenue now and is guided at 16-18% for FY27. Customers plan 3-6 months ahead, with 10-12 month pipeline discussions with larger customers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of automotive lighting and the OEM path?
qa_highlights.answer: Aftermarket production began in May/June 2026 with five leading brands. OEM onboarding is planned for Phase 2, targeted by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be raised given stronger growth in the other business?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management kept the 18-20% FY27 growth guidance, citing volatility, and will revisit at end-Q2 or Q3.

risks_watch: Gross margin (about 41%) sustainability: management says it holds only if raw material prices stay where they are today and the war does not escalate or widen to more countries.

Semiconductor and component lead times: one part ordered in January is still undelivered, and the company is redesigning products to avoid shortages, which could affect yields, costs and customer approvals.
Middle East/UAE: the war cost roughly Rs 10-15 crore of business in Q1 and UAE/Gulf revenue declined YoY; recovery depends on the conflict settling.
Tax rate volatility: Q1 effective tax was around 35%, and management attributed it to deferred tax reversal without giving a sustainable rate.

Hearables and wearables and automotive aftermarket ramp: H&W is about 15-16% of revenue and guided at 16-18% for FY27; automotive lighting FY27 contribution is expected to be small and OEM onboarding is targeted for FY28. Watch for order schedules and the Tower-3 capex (about Rs 20 crore) and depreciation from Tower-2 starting Q2 FY27.
key_quotes: The problem with the gross margins today is we are in times which I would say is similar to what happened during COVID because lead times have gone up like anything.
So, that is why it is safe to say that what we are looking at the way the business is progressing 17% to 18% is what seems feasible.
So, I would stick to the guidance that we had given during quarter 4, which was close to around 18%-20% of growth in the revenue.

So, even if where we are today in terms of raw material pricing, we should still be able to maintain this gross level going forward, unless there is something which is, the war escalates or there are more countries getting involved, something like that.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on diversification, customer additions and the home lighting ODM recovery, but cautious on margins and guidance, repeatedly citing war-driven volatility as the reason for keeping FY27 growth guidance at 18-20% and not raising it. On tax and some business-specific questions (Gravus/Luminati, solar inverter, Honeywell timelines, OEM onboarding) answers were general and gave few numbers.
